# TrackPad.jl

> General Julia library for accelerator tracking, optics, PALS/MAD-X
> interchange, optional GPU batches, Enzyme derivatives, and PolySeries TPSA.

## Canonical documentation

- Human quick start: README.md
- Workflow guide: docs/src/guide.md
- Normative conventions: docs/src/conventions.md
- Element constructors: docs/src/elements.md
- File interchange: docs/src/io.md
- GPU and derivatives: docs/src/gpu.md
- Agent API contract: docs/src/agent-guide.md
- Repository change rules: AGENTS.md
- Generated API reference: docs/src/api.md

## Core contract

- Julia >= 1.12.
- Coordinate order: (x, px, y, py, z, delta).
- Coordinates use metres and normalized momenta.
- Beam(energy) takes total energy in eV; Beam(kinetic=K) / Beam(pc=P0c) for the
  other forms; kinetic_energy(beam), p0c(beam) read them back.
- Scalar CPU tracking is the behavioral reference.
- Public APIs use typed Julia values; do not depend on consumer wrappers.
- Lattice(elements) is open; use periodic=true only for a closed ring.
- Unsupported GPU physics is rejected while constructing GPULattice.
- In-memory PALS envelope: schema `trackpad.pals.branch`, version 1.

## Task to API

- Tracking: track(lat, r_or_coords, beam; nturns=1) and track!(coords, lat, beam; nturns=1, lost=nothing, threaded=false); nturns>1 needs a periodic lattice; lost particles come back as NaN
- Packed CPU/GPU matrix: GPULattice, gpu_adapt, then track!(coords, gl; nturns)
- JuTrack-compatible single pass: linepass(lat, SVector{6}, beam), linepass!(coords, lat, beam, lost_flags) (flags, coordinates kept on loss)
- Parameter sweep: ParamSweepLattice, param_sweep_linepass!
- Tunes/chromaticity: gettune, getchrom (about the off-momentum closed orbit; dQ/d deltaP)
- Optics: twiss(lat, beam; entrance=nothing) -> TwissResult. Ring (no entrance; periodic_twiss): Twiss, dispersion, alphac, slip, chromaticity; second_order=true, radiation_integrals=true, detuning=true add xi2, I1-I5, dQ/dJ; method=:tpsa (default) uses PolySeries Taylor maps, method=:fd finite differences of tracking
- Line: twiss(lat, beam; entrance=optics4DUC or TwissResult) / transport_twiss propagates beta, alpha, phase, dispersion; ring-only fields are nothing
- Sampling inside elements: slices=n, max_step=ds, sample_integrator_steps=true (same keywords on refine_lattice)
- Maps: transfer_map for either boundary; one_turn_map for a ring
- Closed orbit: find_closed_orbit_4d, find_closed_orbit_6d
- PALS subset: read_pals, write_pals
- MAD-X subset: read_madx
- Derivatives: batch_jacobian!, batch_hessian_vector_product!, batch_hessian!
- TPSA: tpsa_map (PolySeries is a dependency)

## Constructor signatures

- Drift(L; kwargs...)
- Quadrupole(L, k1; kwargs...)
- Sextupole(L, k2; kwargs...)
- Octupole(L, k3; kwargs...)
- SBend(L, angle, e1=0, e2=0; kwargs...)
- RBend(L, angle; kwargs...)
- RFCavity(L, volt, freq, lag=0; energy, charge, kwargs...)
- Corrector(L, hkick, vkick; kwargs...)
- Solenoid(L, ks; kwargs...)

## Important semantics

- The stored delta is delta_E = (E - E0) / (P0*c). The interface speaks
  delta_P = (P - P0) / P0: dp arguments, getchrom and the dispersion of
  periodic_twiss are relative momentum (wrt=:deltae opts out); coordinate
  vectors stay delta_E.
- getchrom and every momentum derivative of periodic_twiss are about the off-momentum closed orbit; there is no on-axis option.
- z = s/beta0 - c*t = -c*(t - t0) in metres and is positive for an early
  particle. The longitudinal canonical pair is (z, delta_E).
- Sextupole k2 and octupole k3 are not pre-divided by factorials.
- RF phase = -2*pi*freq*(z+lag)/c - philag.
- RF kicks use signed charge*voltage/(P0*c), not voltage/(K0*beta0^2).
- Direct RFCavity default energy is zero, which disables its kick.
- `check_lost` also checks transverse coordinate/momentum limits, not only NaN.
- `twissline` is the historic name of `periodic_twiss` (Taylor maps by default, `method=:fd` for finite differences).

## Optional backends

- Metal: Float32 only.
- CUDA: Float32 and Float64.
- Enzyme: batched Jacobian; second derivatives use finite differences of
  Enzyme Jacobians in the current implementation.
- PolySeries: hard dependency; TPSA backend of the default optics method.

## Boundaries

Do not invent support for coupled optics, unsupported GPU elements, full MAD-X
language semantics, or exact nested-Enzyme GPU Hessians. Check the relevant
guide and current source before answering. Application topology, engine policy,
serialization, sessions, and UI belong to consumer adapters.
